author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This function reconstructs a **string from its Longest Common Prefix (LCP) array**, which encodes the length of matching prefixes between every pair of suffixes. The algorithm works in two phases: **construction** and **validation**. First, it builds the string by iterating through each position—if a position hasn't been assigned a character yet, it assigns the next letter starting from `'a'`, then propagates that same character to all later positions where `lcp[i][j] > 0` (indicating they should share a prefix with position `i`). If it runs out of letters (exceeds `'z'`), it returns an empty string. Second, it **validates** the constructed string by checking that the LCP values match the actual suffixes: if two positions have **different characters**, their LCP must be `0`; if either position is at the string's end, their LCP must be `1`; otherwise, the LCP at `(i, j)` must equal the LCP at `(i+1, j+1)` plus `1`. If any validation fails, it returns an empty string; otherwise, it returns the constructed word joined together.

author: Vitor
aiExplanation: This code constructs a **string** from a **Longest Common Prefix (LCP) matrix** that specifies how many characters match between each pair of positions. The **first loop** greedily assigns characters starting from `'a'`, incrementing to the next letter when needed—if position `i` is unassigned and `lcp[i][j] > 0` for some `j > i`, it assigns the same character to both positions since they must share a prefix. The **second loop** validates that the constructed string satisfies all LCP constraints: if two positions have **different characters**, their LCP value must be **0** (no match); if they're the **same character**, the LCP must be **1** if either position is at the end of the string, or otherwise equal to `lcp[i+1][j+1] + 1` (extending the common prefix one character deeper). If any constraint is violated, it returns an empty string; otherwise, it returns the constructed word joined together.

aiExplanation: The code constructs a string that matches a given **longest common prefix (LCP) matrix**. It starts by assigning characters sequentially from **'a'** onwards to each unassigned position in the word, and propagates the same character to any subsequent positions that should match (based on `lcp` values). Then it validates the constructed word against the LCP matrix through a backwards scan: if two positions have **different characters**, their `lcp[i][j]` must be **0**; if either position is at the end, `lcp[i][j]` must be **1** (matching only the character itself); otherwise, `lcp[i][j]` must equal **`lcp[i+1][j+1] + 1`** (their common prefix extends one position beyond the next positions' match). If the word uses more than 26 letters (running out of the alphabet) or any constraint fails, it returns an empty string; otherwise, it returns the constructed word joined together.
